groceries_note.text: Most states exempt groceries from the sales tax; some tax them at a reduced rate and a few at the full rate (Tax Foundation, Midyear 2026). Per-state grocery treatment in 'consumption[].groceries' combines the Tax Foundation table as of 2020-01-01 with later changes verified from state revenue departments / Tax Foundation: Kansas (0% from 2025), Oklahoma (state 0% from 2024-08-29), Arkansas and Illinois (state 0% from 2026), Alabama (2% from 2025-09-01), Mississippi (5% from 2025-07-01), Virginia (1%), Tennessee (4%). 'Exempt' refers to state-level treatment; local taxes on groceries may apply in some states.

oecd_tax_wedge_us.household: single, no children, 100% of average wage
oecd_tax_wedge_us.note: OECD 'income tax' includes federal + state + local income taxes for the OECD's representative US worker; useful as a sanity check for the 'Provável' scenario of a single average earner.

scenario_guidance.status: methodology suggestion, not a sourced figure
scenario_guidance.text: Federal income tax and FICA are deterministic given income and filing status (same in all scenarios unless the user's deductions are unknown: Conservador could use the standard deduction plus any OBBBA deductions the user plausibly qualifies for; Elevado the standard deduction only). State income tax: Conservador = user's state with local income tax ignored; Provável = state top/brackets plus TF average local effective rate where listed; Elevado = add the max local income tax. Sales tax on taxable spending: Conservador = state rate only and groceries treated per state rule; Provável = combined (state + population-weighted avg local) rate; Elevado = state rate + max local rate.
